html:
The Maricopa, who call themselves Piipaash, are a Native people of southern Arizona who speak a Yuman language. In 1492 their ancestors lived further down the Gila and Colorado rivers; over the 1700s and 1800s they moved up the Gila River to live beside the Akimel O'odham, or Pima.

The two peoples farmed the river with irrigation, as the Hohokam had done before them, and fought together against the Quechan and Mojave. In 1857 the Maricopa and Pima defeated a Quechan and Mojave war party at the Battle of Pima Butte, one of the last great Native battles of the Southwest. Today the Maricopa share the Gila River Indian Community and the Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community near Phoenix. Their women are known for polished red pottery.
